2026-05-06 — three sessions today. Release shipped + post-release residue cleaned + info-only sizing of remaining v1.0.0 work.

RELEASE STATE:
- v1.0.0-beta.1 SHIPPED: tag 0238934, GitHub release 2026-05-07T03:46Z, all 4 platform binaries, Homebrew tap auto-updated, install verified locally.
- Install paths confirmed live for tomorrow's other-machine soak: GitHub release ✓, tag on origin ✓, Homebrew tap rvr-beta.rb ✓. NPM @seabear/reverie NOT published (registry has 0 versions) — Homebrew or direct binary download only.

DONE TODAY (3 commits, all on origin/main):
- dec9547 rebrand(residue): CODEX_TMPFILE → RVR_TMPFILE; init help text; stress-test cutover; README/release-checklist/ROADMAP prose.
- 3187657 rebrand(residue): directoryStore.ts + config.ts comment-noun cleanup; .reverie/project.name + project.repo refreshed.
- 56d19e9 build(deps): npm audit fix — hono 4.12.16, ip-address 10.1.1. 0 vulns.
- 1392/1392 tests, build, lint clean throughout.

INFO-ONLY THIS SESSION (no commits, two new Reverie entries):
- project.bunMigrationScope: sized both Bun migrations. Binary build (SEA → bun build --compile) is half-day, in v1.0.0-beta.2 scope. Test runner (vitest → bun:test) is 2-4 days, dominated by vi.mock auto-hoist restructuring across 31 files; defer to v1.1+. Greenfield rewrite evaluated and rejected.
- project.storeResidueC: C-bucket residue audit — Reverie store itself contains ~25 entries with stale codex_* tool names, CODEX_* env vars, and .codexcli/ paths described as CURRENT state. The B-bucket sweep this morning covered code/CI/docs/tests but missed the store. Effort 1-2 hr mechanical. Full target list categorized in the entry. Do before v1.0.0 stable.

NEXT SESSION PICKS UP (in priority order):
1. Soak the .codexcli/ → .reverie/ auto-migration on a real non-trivial existing store outside this repo (carryover from morning handoff; this repo's own migration during impl session doesn't count).
2. C-bucket store-residue sweep (project.storeResidueC). Mechanical, parallelizable. Verify with `rvr_find codex` returning only the explicit legitimate-historical entries.
3. After soak + sweep, decide v1.0.0-beta.2 (Bun commit-phase via project.bunMigrationScope + short-flag audit) vs jump to v1.0.0 stable.

REBRAND RESIDUE AUDITS — STATUS:
- A-bucket (functional code paths): cleared in surface rebrand v1.0.0-beta.0
- B-bucket (back-compat references like src/utils/paths.ts, src/store.ts, .gitignore, migration tests, CHANGELOG, design docs): reviewed and confirmed legitimate. NOT residue. Don't re-audit.
- C-bucket (Reverie store self-references): IDENTIFIED 2026-05-06 evening, NOT YET SWEPT. See project.storeResidueC.

PARKED (do NOT reopen unless user does):
- bun.lock + .mcp.json untracked — Phase 2 decisions.
- Legacy ccli.rb / ccli-beta.rb formulas in homebrew-reverie tap — separate repo, queued for v1.0.0 stable cleanup.
- rvr migrate-claude-md command — deferrable post-launch.

OPEN WORKSTREAMS USER MAY PICK UP:
- Phase 4 commercial: SeaBear product page, consulting tier/pricing, inquiry response template, Reverie for Teams landing.
- Phase 5 launch: blog post (bicameral story + codexCLI → Reverie narrative), Dogfooding Part Three, GitHub-inbound outreach.
- Workstream 3 visual: logo/wordmark, color palette, marketing site at seabear.dev/reverie.

GOTCHAS:
- The "remote: GitHub found 3 vulnerabilities" message on push after 56d19e9 was a stale Dependabot snapshot — auto-closed shortly after.
- git tag <name> creates lightweight tags; after git push origin main --follow-tags, also push the tag explicitly. (Bit us on v1.0.0-beta.0.)
- npm @seabear/reverie isn't published — if soak plan involves npm install, that path is closed; use Homebrew or direct binary download.

DON'T (next bootstrap):
- Re-do work in dec9547 / 3187657 / 56d19e9.
- Re-audit B-bucket back-compat references — already cleared.
- Cut another release tag autonomously — user-driven moment.
- Re-derive bun migration scope or store-residue list — both saved as project.bunMigrationScope and project.storeResidueC.

USER STATE: Three productive sessions on 2026-05-06 — shipped v1.0.0-beta.1, cleaned post-release residue, sized remaining work and surfaced the C-bucket finding. Steady, controlled cadence. Tomorrow's expectation: real-world soak verification on a different machine.
